en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 3.2.
Hetugocchaka, Kusalattika (The Wholesome Triplet within the Group on Causes)
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root, Object, and With-root. Dependent on a wholesome state that has a root, a wholesome state with a root arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a wholesome state with root-cause, a wholesome state with root-cause arises by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated. One [condition] in the case of root-cause;
one in the case of object; one in the case of predominance; one in the case of proximity; one in the case of contiguity;
one in the case of co-nascence; one in the case of mutuality; one in the case of support; one in the case of decisive support; one in the case of prenascence; one in the case of repetition.
One [condition] in kamma; one in nutriment … pe … one in non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on a wholesome state with root-cause, a wholesome state with root-cause arises by the not-predominance condition. (Abbreviated.)

One by way of non-predominance, one by way of non-prenascence, one by way of non-postnascence, one by way of non-repetition, one by way of non-kamma, one by way of non-resultant, one by way of non-dissociation.
(Abbreviated. One by way of root-condition and non-predominance. (Abbreviated.
One by way of non-predominance-condition and root. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence.
3.2.2.1.7. Chapter of Questions:
The Tetrad of Conditions.
Root-object Condition:
A wholesome state accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state accompanied by roots.
A wholesome state accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state accompanied by roots. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-cause condition: one; object condition: one; predominance condition: one; proximity condition: one; contiguity condition:
one; conascence condition: one; mutuality condition: one; dependence condition: one; strong-dependence condition: one; repetition condition: one; kamma condition: one; nutriment condition:
one; faculty condition: one; jhāna condition: one; path condition: one; association condition: one; presence condition: one; absence condition: one.
One [condition] with regard to the vanished, one with regard to the non-vanished, and one with regard to the non-vanished. (Abbreviated.
Reverse Extraction:

A wholesome state accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state accompanied by roots; it is a condition by way of conascence-condition; it is a condition by way of decisive support-condition.
One by way of not-root; one by way of not-object. (Abbreviated.
One by way of root-condition, not-object; one. (Abbreviated.
One by way of not-root-condition, object; one. (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the Section on Questions in the Wholesome Triplet, so too should they be calculated here.
3.2.2.2. Unwholesome Category 3.2.2.2.1–6. Section on “Dependent on,” etc.
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root, Object, and Root-conditioned. Dependent on a root-conditioned unwholesome state, a root-conditioned unwholesome state arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a rootless unwholesome state, a rooted unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a rooted unwholesome state and a rootless unwholesome state, a rooted unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a rooted unwholesome state, a rooted unwholesome state arises by way of object condition.
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome with root-cause, a state that is unwholesome without root-cause arises by way of object-condition.
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome with root-cause, states that are both unwholesome with root-cause and unwholesome without root-cause arise by way of object-condition.
Dependent on a rootless unwholesome state, a rooted unwholesome state arises by way of object condition.
Dependent on both a rooted unwholesome and a rootless unwholesome state, a rooted unwholesome state arises by way of object condition.
Dependent on a rooted unwholesome state, a rooted unwholesome state arises by way of predominance condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to cause, three; with respect to object, five; with respect to predominance, one; with respect to proximity, five; with respect to contiguity, five;
with respect to conascence, five; with respect to mutuality, five; with respect to dependence, five; with respect to strong-dependence, five;

with respect to prenascence, five; with respect to repetition, five; with respect to kamma, five; with respect to nutriment, five; with respect to faculty, five; with respect to jhāna, five; with respect to path, five.
With respect to association, five; with respect to dissociation, five; with respect to presence, five; with respect to absence, five;
with respect to disappearance, five; with respect to non-disappearance, five. (Abbreviated. Not-root, not-predominance.
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome with root-cause, a state that is unwholesome without root-cause arises by way of the not-root condition (*na-hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is unwholesome with root-cause, a state that is unwholesome with root-cause arises by way of the not-predominance condition (*na-adhipatipaccaya*). (Abbreviated. One [condition] in the case of not-root;

five in the case of not-predominance; five in the case of not-prenascence; five in the case of not-postnascence; five in the case of not-repetition; three in the case of not-kamma; five in the case of not-resultant; five in the case of not-dissociation. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, there are three [answers] for non-predominance condition. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, there is one for object condition. (Abbreviated.
(The sections on conascence, dependence, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on "dependent" [paṭicca]).
3.2.2.2.7. Chapter on Questions (Pañhāvāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka) beginning with Root (Hetu) and Object (Ārammaṇa).
A state with root-cause that is unwholesome is a condition, by way of root-cause condition, for a state with root-cause that is unwholesome … two.
A state with root-cause that is unwholesome is a condition, by way of object condition, for a state with root-cause that is unwholesome … three.
A state without root-cause that is unwholesome is a condition, by way of object condition, for a state without root-cause that is unwholesome … three.
Both faulty states with root-cause and faulty states without root-cause are related to a faulty state with root-cause by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*)—three [instances].
A faulty state with root-cause is related to a faulty state with root-cause by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*): object-predominance and co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*).

(Abbreviated. Two in the case of root-cause; nine in the case of object; one in the case of predominance; nine in the case of immediate; nine in the case of contiguity; nine in the case of co-nascence...
Five [in mutuality], five [in dependence], nine [in decisive support], nine [in repetition], three [in kamma],
three [in nutriment], three [in faculty], three [in jhāna], three [in path], five [in association],
five [in presence], nine [in absence], nine [in disappearance], five [in non-disappearance]. (Abbreviated.)
Negative Extraction:

A conditioned unwholesome state is a condition for a conditioned unwholesome state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), co-nascent condition (*sahajātapaccaya*), and decisive support condition (*upanissayapaccaya*). (Abbreviated. [In the negative permutation: Nine [conditions] are excluded from the root-condition (*na-hetuyā*);
nine [conditions] are excluded from the object-condition (*na-ārammaṇe*). (Abbreviated.)
With root-condition, not-object: two. (Abbreviated.
With not-root-condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive sequences were calculated for the Question Section of the Wholesome Triplet, so too should they be calculated here.)
3.2.2.3. Indeterminate Section (Abyākatapada) 3.2.2.3.1–6. Chapter on Dependence, etc. (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka)
2.2.3.7. Chapter on Questions:
The Tetrad of Conditions—Root Condition (Hetu)
Dependent on a state that is indeterminate with root-cause, a state that is indeterminate with root-cause arises by way of root-condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is indeterminate without root-cause, a state that is indeterminate without root-cause arises by way of root-condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is both indeterminate with root-cause and indeterminate without root-cause, a state that is indeterminate with root-cause arises by way of root-condition … three. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to cause: nine; with respect to object: four; with respect to predominance: five; with respect to proximity: four; with respect to contiguity:
four; with respect to conascence: nine; with respect to mutuality: six ... [etc. ... with respect to prenascence: two; with respect to repetition: two; with respect to kamma:
nine; with respect to result: nine ... [etc. ... with respect to dissociation: nine ... [etc. ... with respect to non-disappearance: nine. (Abbreviated.)
Dependent on a rootless indeterminate state, a rootless indeterminate state arises by way of the not-root condition.
Dependent on a rooted indeterminate state, a rootless indeterminate state arises by way of the not-object condition.
Dependent on a rootless indeterminate state, a rootless indeterminate state arises by way of the not-object condition.
Dependent on both a root-endowed indeterminate state and a rootless indeterminate state, a rootless indeterminate state arises by way of the not-object condition.
Dependent on a root-endowed indeterminate state, a root-endowed indeterminate state arises by way of the not-predominance condition. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root: one; not-object: three; not-predominance: nine; not-proximity:
three; not-contiguity: three; not-mutuality: three; not-strong-dependence: three; not-prenascence: nine; not-postnascence: nine; not-repetition:
nine; not-kamma: two; not-resultant: five; not-nutriment: one; not-faculty: one; not-jhāna: one; not-path: [nine].
One [condition], three for not-association, two for not-dissociation, three for not-absence, and three for not-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
With root-condition, three for not-object. (Abbreviated.
With not-root-condition, one for object. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, dependence, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on "dependent" [paṭicca]).
Root-object: A root-conditioned indeterminate state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a root-conditioned indeterminate state ... three.
A conditioned indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a conditioned indeterminate state.
(Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: four; under predominance: four; under proximity: four; under contiguity:
four; under conascence: seven; under mutuality: six; under dependence: seven; under strong-dependence: four; under prenascence: [four].
Two by postnascence, two by repetition, four by kamma, four by result,
four by nutriment, four by faculty, four by jhāna, three by path, two by association, three by dissociation,
seven by presence … [and so on] … seven by non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
A conditioned indeterminate state is related to a conditioned indeterminate state by way of object condition, conascence condition, and decisive support condition. (Abbreviated.
Seven [conditions] excluding root; seven excluding object. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: four. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive combinations were calculated for the Question Section of the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.)
The "Duality with Cause" and the "Triad of the Wholesome" are completed.
3.2.3. The "Duality of Association with Causes," the "Triad of the Wholesome. 3.2.3.1.
The Section on the Wholesome.
3.2.3.1.1–6 Section on "Dependent" and Other Terms (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions— Root Condition (Hetu)
Dependent on a wholesome state associated with a root, a wholesome state associated with a root arises by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root: one; under object: one; under predominance: one … pe … under non-disappearance: one. (Abbreviated. Negative.

With not-predominance condition: one; with not-prenascence condition: one; with not-postnascence condition: one; with not-repetition condition: one; with not-kamma condition: one; with not-resultant condition: one; with not-dissociation condition: one. (Abbreviated.
With root condition and not-predominance: one. (Abbreviated. With not-predominance condition and root: one. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, dependence, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on "Dependent" [Paṭicca-vāra].
3.2.3.1.7. Question Section (Pañhāvāra):
The Fourfold Conditionality (Paccayacatukka).
Root condition: A wholesome state associated with roots is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state associated with roots. (Abbreviated. Under root: one;
under object: one; under predominance: one; under proximity: one; under contiguity: one … pe … under kamma: one … pe … under non-disappearance: one. (Abbreviated.)
Negative-Exclusion (Paccanīyuddhāra):

A wholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state associated with a root; it is a condition by way of conascence-condition; it is a condition by way of decisive-support-condition.
[In the negative: one [condition] when not-root; one [condition] when not-object. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: one. (Abbreviated. With not-root condition, object: one. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods for the question-section of the Wholesome Triplet were calculated, so should they be calculated here.)
3.2.3.2. Unwholesome Section (Akusala-pada) 3.2.3.2.1–6. The Chapter on Dependence, etc. (Paṭicca-ādi-vāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccaya-catukka)
Root-object condition:
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with a root, an unwholesome state associated with a root arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state dissociated from a root, an unwholesome state associated with a root arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is unwholesome and associated with a root, and dependent on a state that is unwholesome and dissociated from a root, there arises a state that is unwholesome and associated with a root, by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is unwholesome and associated with a root, there arises a state that is unwholesome and associated with a root, by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*)—three [cases].
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome and dissociated from a root, there arises a state that is unwholesome and associated with a root, by way of the object-condition.
Dependent on unwholesome states associated with roots and unwholesome states dissociated from roots, an unwholesome state associated with roots arises by way of object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with roots, an unwholesome state associated with roots arises by way of predominance condition (*adhipati-paccaya*). (Abbreviated.
There are three [conditions] for root; five for object; one for predominance; five for immediate; five for contiguity.
In co-nascence, five; in mutuality, five; in dependence, five; in strong-dependence, five; in prenascence, five; in repetition, five;
in kamma, five; in nutriment, five; in faculty, five; in jhāna, five; in path, five;
in association, five; in dissociation, five; in presence, five …pe… in non-disappearance, five. (Abbreviated.)
Not-root, not-predominance:
dependent on a root-associated unwholesome state, there arises a root-dissociated unwholesome state by way of the not-root condition.
Dependent on a root-associated unwholesome state, there arises a root-associated unwholesome state by way of the not-predominance condition. (Abbreviated.)

With not-root condition: one; with not-predominance: five; with not-prenascence: five; with not-postnascence: five; with not-repetition: five; with not-kamma: three; with not-resultant: five; with not-dissociation: five. (Abbreviated.
With root condition and not-predominance: three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition and object: one. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, dependence, association, and conjunction are to be expanded in detail according to the method of the "Dependent" section.
3.2.3.2.7. The Question Section:
The Fourfold Conditionality.
Root-object condition:
An unwholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state associated with a root… two.
An unwholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state associated with a root… three.
An unwholesome state dissociated from roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state dissociated from roots… three.

Unwholesome states both associated with roots and dissociated from roots are conditions, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state associated with roots… three. (Abbreviated. In the root [condition], two;

in the object [condition], nine; in the predominance [condition], one; in the proximity [condition], nine; in the contiguity [condition], nine; in the conascence [condition]… [The text continues with further enumerations of conditions.]
With respect to the five [objects], there are five [conditions] through mutuality; five through dependence; nine through decisive support; nine through repetition; three through kamma;
three through nutriment; three through faculty; three through jhāna; three through path; five through association;
five through presence …pe… five through non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
Negative Extraction:

An unwholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for an unwholesome state associated with a root; it is a condition by way of conascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*); it is a condition by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*).
(Abbreviated. [In the negative analysis: nine [conditions] excluding the root-cause; nine excluding the object. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: two. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive combinations were calculated for the Question Section of the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.)
3.2.3.3. Indeterminate Section (Abyākatapada) 3.2.3.3.1–6. The Chapter on Dependence, etc. (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka)
Dependent on a root-associated indeterminate state, a root-associated indeterminate state arises by way of the root condition... three.
Dependent on a root-dissociated indeterminate state, a root-dissociated indeterminate state arises by way of the root condition... three.

Dependent on a state that is both associated with a root and indeterminate, and a state that is dissociated from a root and indeterminate, there arises a state that is associated with a root and indeterminate by way of root-condition … three.
(Abbreviated. Nine for root; four for object; five for predominance; four for proximity; four for contiguity; nine for conascence;
six for mutuality … pe … two for prenascence; two for repetition; nine for kamma; nine for result.
… pe … nine with respect to the path, four with respect to association, nine with respect to dissociation … pe … nine with respect to non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
Not-root, not-object: In dependence on a root-dissociated indeterminate state, a root-dissociated indeterminate state arises by way of the not-root condition.
Dependent on a neutral state associated with a root, there arises a neutral state dissociated from a root by way of the not-object condition. (Abbreviated. [In the negative analysis:

one for not-root, three for not-object, nine for not-predominance, three for not-proximity, three for not-contiguity, three for not-mutuality, three for not-strong-dependence, nine for not-prenascence, nine for not-postnascence, [nine] for not-repetition...
Nine; with respect to not-kamma, two; with respect to not-resultant, five; with respect to not-nutriment, one; with respect to not-faculty, one;

with respect to not-jhāna, one; with respect to not-path, one; with respect to not-association, three; with respect to not-dissociation, two; with respect to not-absence, three; with respect to not-disappearance, three. (Abbreviated.
With root condition and not-object, three. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, there is one [answer] for the object [condition]. (Abbreviated.
(The sections on conascence, dependence, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on "dependent" [paṭicca]).
3.2.3.3.7. The Chapter of Questions (Pañhāvāra).
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root and Object.
A root-associated indeterminate state is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a root-associated indeterminate state. … [Three.]
An indeterminate state associated with a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state associated with a root. (Abbreviated.

[There are] three in the case of root, four in the case of object, four in the case of predominance, four in the case of proximity, four in the case of contiguity, seven in the case of conascence, six in the case of mutuality, seven in the case of dependence, four in the case of strong-dependence, and [four] in the case of prenascence.
In the case of post-nascence and repetition, there are two; in kamma, four; in result, four; in nutriment, faculty, and jhāna, four;
in path, three; in association, two; in dissociation, three ... pe ... in non-disappearance, seven.
(Abbreviated. Negative Enumeration.

An indeterminate state associated with a root is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for an indeterminate state associated with a root; it is a condition by way of co-nascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*); it is a condition by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*).
[In the negative permutation: seven [conditions] excluding root; seven excluding object. (Abbreviated.
With root-condition, three [conditions] excluding object. (Abbreviated.)
With non-root condition, there are four [answers] regarding the object-condition. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the question-section of the wholesome triad, so should they be calculated here.
The Wholesome Triad of the Root-Associated Pair is finished.
3.2.4. The Dyads on With Cause and Without Cause; The Triads on the Wholesome. 3.2.4.1.
The Section on the Wholesome.
3.2.4.1.1–6. The Chapter on "Dependent," etc.
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by a root, there arises a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by a root, by way of the root condition... [three].
Dependent on a wholesome state that is both with cause and not itself a cause, there arises a wholesome state that is both with cause and not itself a cause, by way of root condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is both a root and with cause and wholesome, and a state that is both with cause and not itself a root and wholesome, there arises a state that is both a root and with cause and wholesome, by way of root condition … three.
(Abbreviated. Nine for root; nine for object … pe … nine for kamma; nine for nutriment … pe … nine for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)

Dependent on a wholesome state that is neither-predominance-nor-root and is with-root, there arises a wholesome state that is neither-predominance-nor-root and is with-root, by way of the not-predominance condition.

(Abbreviated. Nine for not-predominance; nine for not-prenascence; nine for not-postnascence; nine for not-repetition; three for not-kamma; nine for not-resultant; nine for not-dissociation. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, there are nine [answers] for non-predominance. (Abbreviated.
With non-predominance condition, there are nine for root. (Abbreviated.
(The sections on co-nascence, dependence, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on "dependent" [paṭicca].)
3.2.4.1.7. Chapter on Questions:
The Tetrad of Conditions—Root Condition (Hetu)
A wholesome state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a wholesome state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause.
(Abbreviated. [There are] three in the case of the root; nine in the case of the object; nine in the case of the predominance; nine in the case of the immediate; nine in the case of the contiguous;

nine in the case of the conascence; nine in the case of the mutuality; nine in the case of the support; nine in the case of the decisive support; nine in the case of the repetition; three in the case of the kamma; [three] in the case of the nutriment...
Three; with respect to faculties, nine; with respect to jhāna, three; with respect to the path, associated, nine ... pe ... non-disappearance, nine.
(Abbreviated. Negative Extraction:
A wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is related to a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots.
It is a condition by way of object-condition … by way of conascence-condition … by way of decisive support-condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine [instances] excluding root; nine excluding object. (Abbreviated.
With root-condition, three excluding object. (Abbreviated.)
With non-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object condition. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive enumerations were calculated for the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.
3.2.4.2. Unwholesome Section.
3.2.4.2.1–6 Section on "Dependent" and Other Terms (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions— Root Condition (Hetu)
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, an unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots arises by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of the root; nine in the case of the object … pe … nine in the case of kamma; nine in the case of nutriment … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance.
(Abbreviated. Not-predominance.
Dependent on a root-and-rooted unwholesome state, a root-and-rooted unwholesome state arises by way of the not-predominance condition (*na-adhipati-paccaya*) … nine.

(Abbreviated. Nine for not-predominance; nine for not-prenascence; nine for not-postnascence; nine for not-repetition; three for not-kamma; nine for not-resultant; nine for not-dissociation. (Abbreviated.
With root-condition, nine for not-predominance. (Abbreviated.)
With non-predominance condition and root condition, there are nine. (Abbreviated.
(The sections on conascence, dependence, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on "dependent" [paṭicca]).
3.2.4.2.7. Question Section (Pañhāvāra)
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root.

An unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by a root is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a state that is both a root and accompanied by a root and is unwholesome. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-condition: three; with respect to object-condition: nine ... pe ... with respect to repetition-condition: nine; with respect to kamma-condition: three; with respect to nutriment-condition: three; with respect to faculty, jhāna, and path-conditions: three; with respect to association-condition: nine ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance-condition: nine. (Abbreviated. Exclusion of the Negative (Paccanīyuddhāra):
